full_judgment:
4. On behalf of the Government it was stated that the properties in question were situated within the periphery of the hat and bazar locally called Sultanpur bazar, Further, the plots and structures were acquired by the Government under sections 3(1) and 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, by a General Notification issued on April 2, 1956. The right and title of the land vested in the Government with effect from April 14, 1962. It might be that the local Tahshildar realised rent from the appellant and granted him provisional rent receipts but they did not create any right and title of the appellant. Plot Nos. 12446, 12447 and 12448 are definitely situated within the periphery of Sultanpur bazar and were, therefore not retainable class of land under section 20(2) of the Act read with Ordinance No. 12 of 1960. 

 "The land with structures on plot Nos. 12446, 12447 and 1244 is definitely situated within the periphery of Sultanpur bazar within the meaning of section 2(12) of the said Act and it is not a retain able class of land under section 20(2) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with Ordinance No. 12 of 1960." 

 7. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the High Court Division the appellant moved this Court and obtained leave to consider whether the properties in question being situated within the periphery of the hat and bazar as claimed by the respondents came within the meaning of hat and bazar under section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and whether word 'periphery' would include the properties in question as being within the hat and bazar. 

 "Seen the report of the R.C.O. and the sketch map showing area proposed to be classified as bazar, I personally went to the locality, and personally inspected the area. The area shown in the sketch map in red attested by the R.C.O. and R.V.W. signed by me should be classified bazar and bat area for the purpose of determining' non-retainable khas land under section 20 of the State. Acquisition and Tenancy Act, The S.D.S.O. should finalise the case and the R.C.O. should correct the record accordingly and prepare compensation for the persons concerned."
